# `silk/system/host_input`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The `HostInput` effect: the command-line arguments, environment variables, and working directory
of the process, as bytes.

## When to use
Require `&mut HostInput` in code that reads process arguments or environment variables, so a
test can provide its own values. Use [`HostInput.text`](#HostInput.impl.text) when you need text. Keep the bytes when
you only pass a value on, because a host value is not always valid UTF-8.

## Details
Argument 0 is the program name. The arguments keep the order of the host. A missing argument
index or an unset variable gives an absent `Option`, not an error. Each returned value is an
owned `Bytes`, so the lookups need an `Allocator`.

This effect only reads. It does not change environment variables or the working directory.

## Errors
- [`HostInputError`](#HostInputError) if the provider cannot answer.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply a returned value.

## Examples
### Provide arguments in a test
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.collections.bytes { Bytes }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.system.host_input { HostInput, HostInputError }
import silk.option { Option }

struct FixedInput {}

effect fn argumentCount(self: &mut FixedInput) -> usize
  ! HostInputError {
  return 2
}

effect fn argument(self: &mut FixedInput, index: usize) -> Option<Bytes>
  ! HostInputError | OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator {
  if index == 1 {
    return Option<Bytes>.some(run Bytes.copy(&b"--verbose"))
  }
  return Option<Bytes>.none()
}

effect fn variable(self: &mut FixedInput, name: &[u8]) -> Option<Bytes>
  ! HostInputError | OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator {
  return Option<Bytes>.none()
}

effect fn workingDirectory(self: &mut FixedInput) -> Bytes
  ! HostInputError | OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator {
  return run Bytes.copy(&b"/")
}

impl HostInput for FixedInput {
  argumentCount: FixedInput.argumentCount

  argument: FixedInput.argument

  variable: FixedInput.variable

  workingDirectory: FixedInput.workingDirectory
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! HostInputError | OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut provider = FixedInput {}
  let flag = run HostInput.argument(1) |> Effect.provideMut<HostInput>(&mut provider)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let length = match move flag {
    Option<Bytes>.Some { value } => Bytes.length(&value)
    Option<Bytes>.None => 0
  }
  if length != 9 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="HostInput"></a>

## `HostInput`

```silk
pub service HostInput
```

The effect that reads process arguments, environment variables, and the working directory, as
bytes.

### When to use

Require `&mut HostInput` in code that reads process arguments or environment variables, so a
test can provide its own values. Use [`HostInput.text`](#HostInput.impl.text) when you need text. Keep the bytes when
you only pass a value on, because a host value is not always valid UTF-8.

### Details

Argument 0 is the program name. The arguments keep the order of the host. This effect only
reads. It does not change environment variables or the working directory. Each returned value is
an owned `Bytes`, so the lookups need an `Allocator`.

An absent argument and an unset variable are normal answers, so they give an absent `Option`.
Only a provider that cannot answer fails with [`HostInputError`](#HostInputError). Each returned value is owned
by the caller.

<a id="HostInput.argumentCount"></a>

### Operation `argumentCount`

```silk
effect fn argumentCount() -> usize ! HostInputError ? &mut HostInput
```

Returns the number of arguments, including the program name at index 0.

#### Errors

- [`HostInputError`](#HostInputError) if the provider cannot read the arguments.

<a id="HostInput.argument"></a>

### Operation `argument`

```silk
effect fn argument(
    index: usize
  ) -> Option<Bytes> ! HostInputError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut HostInput | &mut Allocator
```

Returns a copy of argument `index` as bytes. Returns an absent option if `index` is not less
than the argument count.

#### Errors

- [`HostInputError`](#HostInputError) if the provider cannot read the arguments.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the copy.

<a id="HostInput.variable"></a>

### Operation `variable`

```silk
effect fn variable(
    name: &[u8]
  ) -> Option<Bytes> ! HostInputError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut HostInput | &mut Allocator
```

Returns a copy of the value of the environment variable `name`. Returns an absent option if
the variable is not set.

#### Errors

- [`HostInputError`](#HostInputError) if the provider cannot read the environment.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the copy.

<a id="HostInput.workingDirectory"></a>

### Operation `workingDirectory`

```silk
effect fn workingDirectory() -> Bytes ! HostInputError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut HostInput | &mut Allocator
```

Returns a copy of the working directory path as bytes.

#### Errors

- [`HostInputError`](#HostInputError) if the provider cannot read the working directory.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the copy.

<a id="HostInput.impl.variableNamed"></a>

### Associated function `variableNamed`

```silk
pub effect fn variableNamed(
    name: string
  ) -> Option<Bytes> ! HostInputError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut HostInput | &mut Allocator
```

Returns a copy of the value of the environment variable `name`. Returns an absent option if
the variable is not set.

#### When to use

Use it for a name that is a string literal, such as `"HOME"`. It calls `HostInput.variable`
with the UTF-8 bytes of `name`.

#### Errors

- [`HostInputError`](#HostInputError) if the provider cannot read the environment.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the copy.

<a id="HostInput.impl.arguments"></a>

### Associated function `arguments`

```silk
pub effect fn arguments(
  ) -> List<Bytes> ! HostInputError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut HostInput | &mut Allocator
```

Returns copies of all arguments, in order, with the program name at index 0.

#### When to use

Use it when you need all arguments. Use `HostInput.argument` to read one argument without
copying the others.

#### Errors

- [`HostInputError`](#HostInputError) if the provider cannot read the arguments, or if it reports a count and
  then has no argument for an index below that count.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the copies.

<a id="HostInput.impl.text"></a>

### Associated function `text`

```silk
pub fn text(values: &[u8]) -> Result<string, InvalidUtf8>
```

Returns `values` as a `string` if it is valid UTF-8. It does not copy.

#### When to use

Use it when you need a host value as text, for example to compare an argument with `"--help"`.
To pass a value on, keep the bytes.

#### Errors

- `InvalidUtf8` if `values` is not valid UTF-8. `values` does not change.
